It was good to see some of our younger elements, namely D. Crookes and J. Radford finishing in the first half of a strong field.
Crookes and J. Radford competed Xmas and Boxing Day and on the latter both ran personal bests.
In the Junior race our members finished as follows :- 29, T. Hart; 41, J.
Ken Miller was now 29th, John Thresher 50th, Derek Crookes 92nd and Jim Radford 107th; Trevor Hart being forced to drop back a considerable way with trouble from a shoulder ailment.
For lap after lap, Pat Newell, the holder, Mal Robinson, our Mile Champion, and Jim Radford ran together; neither giving nor expecting quarter.

The mile brought out our two most promising middle distance runners, Jim Radford and John Thresher. It was a good class field and it was to John's credit that he finished fourth in a personal best, 4:21.6.

Jim Radford was a very good second to Maynard (HHH) in the 1½ miles; third place going to Charlie Dabbs, now free from injury. Eric Penny gained a valuable 10 points with a win in the junior ¾ mile, and a walk-over in the 660 yards.
11th Stage.Jim Radford (21.25) This was Jim's first taste of the Brighton road and although his time of 21mins25secs was not outstanding he can be well pleased with his initial run in bad conditions.

Going off down Copse Hill the three leaders were still locked together but the field behind had started to string out, although it was noticed that John Moore, Jim Radford and Archie Bedford who had started slowly were working their way through.
Jim Radford was next to run. Unfortunately, Jim in his enthusiasm set off far too fast and after a mile or so was definitely feeling the pinch.
On the third leg Jim Radford had to give best to Poly's Ralph Dunkley (13:21) and Rooke of Essex Beagles (13:36) and handed over to Derek Crookes fourth.

Most improved runners of the season are at present Ken Miller, Alan Black and, Junior Cyril Forey; but perhaps there are some dark horses waiting for the final run-in before they show their hand---Mike Heck, Jim Radford, David Jones and John Thresher for example.
When the first Hog's Back race was held in 1958 Belgrave just scraped up a team of the bare scoring three:- Derek Crookes, Jim Radford and Alan Bishop.

I was an 880 man and he was a spear chucker but we ran as juniors in the Middlesex cross country championships with Derek Crookes, George Flanagan and Jimmy Radford under the supervision of Bob Taylor, a miler and half miler of some distinction before illness cut his career short.
